text:
sam: heads-up — rolled a small runtime change this morning: "slate" batching + opportunistic KV-squash to prod at 07:05 PT. canary 5% -> 30% -> 100%.

oncall-bot: deploy started: commit d5f7a33 -> prod | canary=5% -> 30% -> 100% | sha d5f7a33 | eta 00:16:00

vivian: quick 20m after-100% snapshot: p50 -7%, p95 -21%, p99 -18%, cost/1k -15%. small win but consistent.

lee: numbers I pulled from dash: 
```
before: {p50: 95ms, p95: 230ms, p99: 480ms, cost_1k: $0.044} 
after:  {p50: 88ms, p95: 182ms, p99: 394ms, cost_1k: $0.037}
```

mike: what is slate batching and KV-squash?

sam: slate batching groups very short requests into tiny fixed windows (2-8ms) but avoids clumping by using jitter + backpressure signals. KV-squash dedupes near-simultaneous KV fetches per-session and coalesces identical shard reads. both are conservative — latency ceiling set so single-request paths unaffected.

oncall-bot: infra note: saw a brief queue rise at the 30% step (~70s) while new batching lanes warmed; autoscaler added one worker for ~2m. no GPU OOMs.

support: any client-side impacts? mobile team reported a handful of 429s during canary.

vivian: 429s came from an old SDK that used tight retry loops; fallback routing handled most. filed INF-11120 to follow up with SDK team.

lee: workload split: short (<=64 tokens) saw biggest cost drop (~20%), medium ~12%, long-context p99 down ~10% but cost delta small.

sam: added a hotfix alert: post-deploy_queue > 110 for >90s -> page eng-sre. PR #5077.

vivian: drafting internal blurb for product: "Typical short-context apps: ~15-25% lower inference unit cost and improved p95 latency. Long-contexts see smaller cost wins but better p99. See internal perf graph."

oncall-bot: deploy finished: commit d5f7a33 -> prod | status=success | duration=00:21:12 :rocket:

mike: nice work, team! will monitor for 48h and flag if p99 regresses. :tada:
